subject: pharmacology
title: Biologic Disease-Modifying Drugs, Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitors, and Urate-Lowering Therapy

steps.tx: A soluble dimeric fusion protein linking the extracellular ligand-binding domain of human TNF receptor 2 to the Fc portion of human IgG1 is **etanercept**. Administered subcutaneously once weekly at 50 mg, etanercept binds and neutralizes both soluble TNF-alpha and lymphotoxin-alpha. Unlike monoclonal antibodies, it does not trigger complement-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, accounting for a significantly lower incidence of latent tuberculosis reactivation. It provides effective disease suppression in active rheumatoid arthritis, polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis.
steps.say: Etanercept is a soluble TNF receptor fusion protein that neutralizes TNF-alpha without inducing complement-mediated cell lysis.

left.title: Etanercept (Soluble Receptor Fusion)
points: Recombinant p75 TNF receptor linked to IgG1 Fc domain
Binds soluble TNF-alpha and lymphotoxin-alpha
Does not trigger complement-dependent cellular lysis
Lower relative risk of latent tuberculosis reactivation

right.title: Infliximab (Chimeric Monoclonal Antibody)
points: Chimeric human-murine IgG1 monoclonal antibody
Binds soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha trimers
Triggers complement cytotoxicity and cellular apoptosis
Higher risk of tuberculosis reactivation and antibody development

steps.tx: The fully human recombinant IgG1-kappa monoclonal antibody directed specifically against human tumor necrosis factor-alpha is **adalimumab**. Administered subcutaneously every two weeks at 40 mg, adalimumab binds soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha with high affinity, preventing receptor binding and downregulating cellular adhesion molecules and vascular endothelial growth factor. Because of its entirely human polypeptide sequence, it exhibits lower immunogenicity than chimeric antibodies, though neutralizing anti-drug antibodies can still attenuate clinical response. Co-administration with weekly methotrexate reduces anti-adalimumab antibody formation.
steps.say: Adalimumab is a fully human anti-TNF monoclonal antibody administered subcutaneously every two weeks.

nodes.label: Subcutaneous adalimumab administration (40 mg every 2 weeks)
High-affinity binding to soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha
Blockade of TNFR1 and TNFR2 downstream NF-kappa-B signaling
Downregulation of synovial adhesion molecules and arrest of bony erosion

steps.tx: A chimeric monoclonal antibody that targets the CD20 surface antigen present on pre-B and mature B lymphocytes is **rituximab**. Administered as two 1000 mg intravenous infusions separated by two weeks and repeated every six months, rituximab depletes circulating B cells via complement-dependent cytotoxicity and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. Indicated for active rheumatoid arthritis refractory to anti-TNF biologics, it disrupts autoantibody production and T-cell costimulation. Pre-treatment screening is mandatory because it can provoke fatal hepatitis B virus reactivation and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.
steps.say: Rituximab depletes CD20-positive B lymphocytes to control severe rheumatoid arthritis refractory to anti-TNF therapy.

rows: Hepatitis B viral serologies and JC virus monitoring
Severe painful injection site cutaneous reactions

steps.tx: A soluble fusion protein comprising the extracellular domain of cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 linked to a modified IgG1 Fc domain is **abatacept**. By selectively binding to CD80 and CD86 costimulatory molecules on antigen-presenting cells, abatacept prevents their interaction with CD28 receptors on naive and memory T lymphocytes. This selective costimulation blockade arrests T-cell activation, suppressing downstream cytokine release, synovial proliferation, and osteoclast activation in rheumatoid arthritis patients who fail conventional DMARDs or anti-TNF agents.
steps.say: Abatacept binds CD80 and CD86 to block costimulatory signal 2, arresting T-cell activation in rheumatoid synovium.

left.title: Antigen-Specific Signal 1
points: MHC class II peptide complex engages T-cell receptor (TCR)
Provides primary antigen recognition specificity
Insufficient alone to trigger productive T-cell proliferation
Absence of signal 2 induces functional immune anergy

right.title: Costimulatory Signal 2 (Targeted by Abatacept)
points: APC surface CD80 and CD86 engage T-cell surface CD28
Drives interleukin-2 transcription, survival, and proliferation
Abatacept mimics CTLA-4 to bind CD80/86 with avid affinity
Selective costimulatory blockade induces immune tolerance

steps.tx: The foundational purine-analogue xanthine oxidase inhibitor utilized as first-line urate-lowering therapy in chronic gout is **allopurinol**. Metabolized by xanthine oxidase into the long-acting active metabolite oxypurinol, it competitively inhibits xanthine oxidase, blocking the sequential oxidation of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid. This lowers serum and urinary uric acid below the 6 mg/dL saturation threshold. It must never be initiated during an acute gout flare, and carriers of the HLA-B*58:01 allele carry extreme risks of fatal severe cutaneous adverse reactions.
steps.say: Allopurinol is metabolized to oxypurinol, inhibiting xanthine oxidase to suppress uric acid formation in chronic gout.

vis.alt: Purine metabolic pathway showing xanthine oxidase and uric acid synthesis
vis.caption: Purine degradation cascade demonstrating xanthine oxidase conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and uric acid, blocked by allopurinol and febuxostat.

steps.tx: A potent non-purine selective inhibitor of xanthine oxidase that achieves robust urate reduction in chronic tophaceous gout is **febuxostat**. Unlike allopurinol, febuxostat forms a tight, stable complex within the catalytic pterin-binding channel of both oxidized and reduced forms of xanthine oxidase without inhibiting other enzymes in purine or pyrimidine metabolism. Because it is eliminated primarily by hepatic glucuronidation and oxidation, febuxostat requires no dosage adjustment in mild-to-moderate renal impairment, making it the preferred xanthine oxidase inhibitor in chronic kidney disease.
steps.say: Febuxostat is a non-purine xanthine oxidase inhibitor cleared hepatically, ideal for gout patients with renal impairment.

left.title: Febuxostat (Non-Purine Inhibitor)
points: Non-purine structure selectively blocks xanthine oxidase
Forms tight complex with both oxidized and reduced enzyme forms
Hepatic metabolism; no dose reduction in moderate renal failure
Higher cardiovascular mortality reported in landmark trials

right.title: Allopurinol (Purine Analogue)
points: Purine analogue oxidized to active metabolite oxypurinol
Blocks only reduced form of xanthine oxidase enzyme
Renal excretion of oxypurinol mandates dose adjustment in CKD
High risk of severe hypersensitivity in HLA-B*58:01 carriers

steps.tx: The crucial clinical principle governing the introduction of xanthine oxidase inhibitors in chronic gout is **urate-lowering therapy initiation**. Starting allopurinol or febuxostat abruptly causes a rapid drop in serum urate concentrations, which destabilizes existing intra-articular monosodium urate tophi and precipitates paradoxical acute gouty arthritis flares. Consequently, urate-lowering drugs must never be started in the midst of an acute flare, and must always be co-prescribed with low-dose prophylactic colchicine or NSAIDs for three to six months to prevent mobilization attacks.
steps.say: Urate-lowering therapy must never start during an acute gout flare and requires anti-inflammatory flare prophylaxis.

nodes.label: Initiation of xanthine oxidase inhibitor (allopurinol or febuxostat)
Rapid precipitous decline in circulating serum uric acid levels
Superficial dissolution and fragmentation of synovial microtophi
Secondary mobilization arthritis flare aborted by co-prescribed colchicine

steps.tx: Mandatory testing for the HLA-B*58:01 allele prior to initiating allopurinol therapy in high-risk populations is **allopurinol pharmacogenomics**. Possessing this human leukocyte antigen allele increases the relative risk of allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome by hundreds of times, provoking severe cutaneous adverse reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, fever, eosinophilia, and acute hepatic and renal failure. The allele frequency is particularly elevated among Han Chinese, Korean, Thai, and African populations, in whom febuxostat serves as the preferred initial urate-lowering agent.
steps.say: Pre-treatment HLA-B*58:01 testing prevents life-threatening allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome in high-risk populations.

rows: Toxic epidermal necrolysis and severe DRESS syndrome
Han Chinese, Korean, Thai, African ancestry
Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
